tools.description: Pattern-based permissions for registered tools. Use exact names or `*` wildcards for canonical Pi built-ins and any extension-provided or third-party tools. Path-bearing built-ins also accept resource-qualified keys such as `read:/home/alice/project/generated/*` or `edit:c:/Users/alice/project/generated/*`.

bash.description: Bash rules as word-prefix lists matched against the normalized argv of every command a bash invocation actually executes (including inside $(...), backticks, bash -c strings, and unwrapped wrappers like timeout/env/xargs). "git diff" covers `git diff --stat HEAD~3`; "rg" covers any rg invocation. Read-only commands are allowed by default via the built-in safe-command registry; precedence per command is deny > protected paths > ask > allow/registry > defaultPolicy.bash.

allow.description: Prefix rules that allow matching commands (subject to protected paths, write policy, and the unsafe-argument guard).

ask.description: Prefix rules that force a prompt even when the registry vouches for the command.

deny.description: Prefix rules that deny matching commands outright.

subshells.description: Subshells `(...)` and brace groups `{ ...; }`. Default: deny.

unanalyzable.description: Parse failures and constructs the analyzer cannot resolve (fails closed). Default: ask.

registryOverrides.description: Safe-command registry adjustments keyed by executable. `null` disables a built-in row; an object replaces or adds one.

protectedPaths.description: Additional protected path patterns (globs matched against every argv token and redirection target, whole or per `/`- and `:`-segment). Matches deny the command, outranking every allow including the registry. Extends built-ins like .env, .ssh, id_rsa*, *.pem.

mcp.description: Pattern-based permissions for targets invoked through a registered `mcp` tool when available.

special.description: Reserved permission checks. The coarse `external_directory` key remains supported, and resource-qualified keys like `external_directory:/home/alice/shared/*` or `external_directory:c:/Users/alice/shared/*` can scope outside-worktree file access by normalized directory resource.

external_directory.description: Coarse fallback for path-bearing file tools when they target paths outside the active working directory.

^external_directory:.+$.description: Resource-qualified external directory rule. Use `external_directory:<normalized-absolute-directory>/*` to allow, deny, or ask for a specific outside directory.
